name: Phú Yên
headline: Golden hour on the coast.
subheadline: Blue sky, stone cliffs, winding roads.
introduction: Phú Yên feels open: long coastal roads, low-key towns, clean horizons, and golden light that makes the landscape look wider than it is.
shortDescription: Stone cliffs, empty roads, blue sky, fishing villages, and one of central Vietnam's quieter coastal moods.
description: A local-led coastal ride through Hòn Yến, Gành Đá Đĩa, Mũi Đại Lãnh, cheap food, and unfairly beautiful roads.
longDescription: The best version of Phú Yên is a road day with space between stops. The coast is the main character, but the quiet transitions between places are where the photos breathe.
overview:
Phú Yên felt almost unfairly beautiful. I was lucky to have a local friend show me around, so I got to see places like Hòn Yến, Gành Đá Đĩa, and Mũi Đại Lãnh without just following a saved map.

Cycling along one of Vietnam's most beautiful coastal roads was a real highlight. The food was cheap, the people were kind, and the whole place had that "I should come back every year" kind of charm.
weatherNote: The dry months are easier for coastal photos. Midday sun can be harsh, so save key stops for softer light.
travelTips: Do fewer stops and give each coastal route time.
Carry water if riding between viewpoints.
Plan around light, not only map distance.
notFor: Travelers who want dense nightlife or a packed city base.

images.title: Black Basalt Wedge at Hòn Yến
images.story: My friend took me out to Hòn Yến before the midday heat took over, pointing out the dark volcanic ridge rising straight out of the turquoise shallows. From the water's edge, the mossy hump looked almost like a resting sea turtle against the cloudless blue sky. The water was remarkably clear, with gentle swells breaking softly against the dark basalt shelf.

images.title: Flagpole Over Mũi Đại Lãnh
images.story: We hiked past the lighthouse and looked down at the outpost perched on the rocky bluff, where the red flag was snapping briskly in the coastal wind. The green hipped roof of the shelter looked toy-sized against the endless blue stretch of the East Sea. My calves were burning from the stone stairs, but the sheer drop and the cool breeze made every step worthwhile.

images.title: Trawlers Between the Sea Cliffs
images.story: Framed between two steep granite bluffs, a trio of blue fishing trawlers motored steadily across the deep sapphire water. Looking straight down through the gap, you could see submerged reefs glowing pale beneath the surface before the shelf plunged into deep ocean. It gave a quiet sense of scale that no wide-angle shot could quite capture.

images.title: Granite Ledges Facing Open Water
images.story: The midday sun was baking the weathered granite boulders along the headland, but the offshore sea breeze kept the air surprisingly crisp. Half a dozen wooden boats were scattered across the calm water, moving at a snail's pace along the coastline. I sat on a flat rock for twenty minutes just watching the light bounce off the open water.

images.title: Baked Terracotta at Tháp Nhạn
images.story: Back in Tuy Hòa, we pulled over at Nhạn Mountain to see this thousand-year-old Cham brick tower standing proudly under the afternoon sun. The deep orange bricks are fitted together without visible mortar, holding up carved pilasters while wild greenery sprouts cheerfully from the roof corners. At the base, a groundskeeper in blue overalls was peacefully watering the flowerbeds, completely unfazed by the centuries looming above him.

images.title: Hexagonal Basalt at Gành Đá Đĩa
images.story: Stepping onto Gành Đá Đĩa feels unreal, with thousands of dark basalt prisms stacked side-by-side like gigantic hexagonal dinner plates. The dark volcanic stone was warm underfoot, and white foamy water surged into the crevices every time a wave broke against the lower edge. It felt like nature's own patio paving, jutting boldly into the bay.

images.title: Three Boats off the Basalt Shelf
images.story: Looking out past the dark basalt columns of Gành Đá Đĩa, three blue fishing boats sat completely still on the deep water. Across the bay, a pale strip of empty beach stretched below the green headland under the midday glare. The salt breeze barely took the edge off the heat, but neither of us was in any hurry to move on.
